options.content:
**Service availability** — one row per probed target (`probe_success` from blackbox_exporter: HTTP checks on every web node, TCP checks on MySQL for every db node). Green = up, red = down. A `systemctl restart nginx`/`mysqld` or a full VM reboot shows up here as a visible red stripe, not just a number that briefly dips.

**Kernel uptime** — `time() - node_boot_time_seconds` per node (`node_exporter`, running natively on every node — web/db/mon, Ubuntu and Oracle Linux alike). Resets to 0 only on an actual reboot; a patched-but-not-rebooted kernel package does not move this. Together the two panels separate two different claims: "the service kept answering" vs. "the host didn't reboot" — a normal `make patch` run should hold the top panel flat while `make patch-reboot` is what resets the bottom one.

panels.title: Service availability
panels.description: probe_success per blackbox target. 1 = up (green), 0 = down (red). Restart or reboot a service and watch this row turn red.

panels.title: Kernel uptime
panels.description: time() - node_boot_time_seconds per node. Only resets on an actual reboot (make patch-reboot) — a patched-but-not-rebooted kernel package does not move this.
